note: Rodent despair tests predicted NMDA antagonists would be antidepressant a decade before ketamine was tried in patients, but the same tests also passed lanicemine and the GluN2B-selective CERC-301, which failed in treatment-resistant depression.
label: Depression (NMDA)

engagement.note: Rats and healthy volunteers both showed dose-dependent gamma-EEG rises; 150 mg lanicemine matched 0.5 mg/kg ketamine, so the dose was declared aligned.
engagement.short: Rat gamma-EEG signature reproduced in volunteers
engagement.quote: Together, these data support the utility of gamma-band EEG as a translational biomarker for NMDA channel blockers, and provide evidence for differentiation of lanicemine from ketamine across multiple end points, including psychotomimetic liability at comparable levels of gamma-EEG.
engagement.confidence: medium: full text read (PMC4195977); gamma-EEG is a downstream pharmacodynamic surrogate, not receptor occupancy; no NMDA occupancy has been measured in any depression trial, and the 2019 esketamine label states the antidepressant mechanism is unknown.
engagement.judgement: Counted a PD biomarker (cortical disinhibition) as engagement because it is the only rodent-to-human target-engagement comparison this class published. Model first use and comparison are the same paper, so the strip opens at 'same'. The 2017 lanicemine failure leaves this cell matched: engagement held, efficacy did not. Side fact not used for status: rodent in-vivo [3H]MK-801 binding (Fernandes 2015, doi 10.1016/j.ejphar.2015.08.044) showed GluN2B antagonists block only ~60% of forebrain NMDA receptors versus ~100% for channel blockers.

dose.model: Rat forced-swim ED50 scaled by GluN2B occupancy
dose.note: CERC-301's human dose (>=8 mg, ~30-50% occupancy) was set from rat FST; both trials at 8-20 mg failed without posting results.
dose.quote: Based on the preclinical and pharmacodynamic data, doses of ≥8 mg in humans are hypothesized to have an acceptable safety profile and result in clinically relevant peak plasma exposure.
dose.confidence: medium: abstract-level; the two CERC-301 trials (NCT01941043 at 8 mg, NCT02459236 at 12/20 mg) have no posted results and no peer-reviewed report, so their failure is known only from sponsor press releases, which the rules do not accept. Ketamine's own 0.5 mg/kg over 40 min was taken from healthy-volunteer psychotomimetic studies (Krystal 1994, doi 10.1001/archpsyc.1994.03950030035004), not from any animal exposure target; esketamine's 56/84 mg came from human dose-ranging.
dose.reason: Trials ran at target; no results posted
dose.judgement: The approved drug (esketamine) used no animal-derived exposure target, so the only model-set dose in the class is CERC-301's occupancy target, which was tested in patients but never published; 'untested' is the honest status. The alternative was an empty cell, which would have hidden that a model-derived target existed.

efficacy.note: AP-7, MK-801 and ACPC mimicked antidepressants in acute mouse despair tests; the prediction preceded any patient test.
efficacy.short: NMDA antagonists antidepressant-like in mouse despair tests
efficacy.quote: These findings indicate that the NMDA receptor complex may be involved in the behavioral deficits induced by inescapable stress, and that substances capable of reducing neurotransmission at the NMDA receptor complex may represent a new class of antidepressants.
efficacy.confidence: high: abstract-level; DOI verified via PubMed (PMID 2171955).

efficacy.note: Seven depressed patients: HDRS fell 14 points within 72 h after 0.5 mg/kg ketamine vs 0 after saline, as the rodent despair tests predicted.
efficacy.quote: These results suggest a potential role for NMDA receptor-modulating drugs in the treatment of depression.
efficacy.confidence: medium: abstract only (paper paywalled). Berman's abstract says 'major depression', not explicitly treatment-resistant; Zarate 2006 (doi 10.1001/archpsyc.63.8.856; NCT00088699, results first posted 2018-10-12) replicated the effect in 18 explicitly treatment-resistant patients.
efficacy.judgement: The generic 'NMDA antagonist = antidepressant' prediction did come from rodents first (1990) and Berman's abstract frames the trial as a test of that preclinical work, so this is a prediction, not a retrodiction; comparison_stated is false because the paper cites the rationale rather than putting model and patient data side by side. But acute FST/TST also score imipramine positive after one dose, so the model could not predict the rapid-onset, week-long effect that is ketamine's actual clinical signal; the rapid-acting models (Li 2010, doi 10.1126/science.1190287: mTOR, Ro 25-6981 in FST/NSFT) were built after Berman/Zarate and retrodicted it. product_in_model is false because Trullas & Skolnick dosed MK-801, AP-7 and ACPC, not ketamine.

efficacy.model: Rodent despair tests + rat gamma-EEG dose alignment
efficacy.note: Lanicemine, dosed to match ketamine's rat/human gamma-EEG signature, failed every endpoint in 302 TRD patients; GluN2B-selective CERC-301 and EVT-101 also failed, unpublished.
efficacy.short: Lanicemine failed despite matched target engagement
efficacy.quote: Although lanicemine was generally well tolerated, neither dose was superior to placebo in reducing depressive symptoms on the primary end point or any secondary measures.
efficacy.confidence: medium: full text read (PMC5312066). The paper compares against its own earlier positive trial (Study 9), not against a model, and the authors attribute the miss to a 13.9-point placebo response. Rodent FST data for lanicemine itself were not found in the peer-reviewed literature (AstraZeneca internal), so the efficacy prediction for lanicemine is class-level.
efficacy.reason: Despair tests pass drugs that fail
efficacy.judgement: Called contra rather than same: the rule says a wrong prediction for any drug in the context overrides matches. The class model (NMDA channel blockers antidepressant-like in despair tests, Trullas 1990) plus the translational gamma-EEG dose alignment (Sanacora 2014) predicted efficacy for lanicemine; a 302-patient trial showed none. No rodent model flagged lanicemine, CERC-301 (rat FST ED50 0.3-0.7 mg/kg at 30-50% occupancy, Garner 2015) or EVT-101 (NCT01128452, terminated n=8) as failures, so 'neg' was never available; the GluN2B-selective traxoprodil had earlier matched (Preskorn 2008, doi 10.1097/JCP.0b013e31818a6cea). Esketamine's TRANSFORM-2 (NCT02418585, results first posted 2019-04-19) is a further match that does not lift the contra under the rules. Year is print year 2017 (epub 2016-09-29).

safety.note: PCP, MK-801 and ketamine vacuolate posterior cingulate/retrosplenial neurons in adult rats at low subcutaneous doses.
safety.short: NMDA antagonists vacuolate rat cortical neurons
safety.quote: These findings raise new questions regarding the safety of these agents in the clinical management of neurodegenerative diseases and reinforce concerns about the potential risks associated with illicit use of PCP.
safety.confidence: high: abstract-level; the model was built on racemic ketamine as a neuroprotectant/anesthetic, and its use for the antidepressant indication dates from the esketamine NDA (submitted 2018-09-04).

safety.note: Racemic ketamine's vacuolation NOAEL is 1.6x the 84 mg AUC; esketamine was negative to 1.8x; no human brain has been examined.
safety.short: Rat lesion margin 1.6x, never checked in humans
safety.quote: The relevance of these findings to humans is unknown.
safety.confidence: high: label section 13.2 text extracted from the FDA PDF (Revised 03/2019); the FDA pharmacology review (211243Orig1s000PharmR.pdf) states 'several dedicated neurotoxicity studies were conducted in rats' and lists only in-vitro NMDAR binding as primary pharmacology, no behavioral antidepressant model.
safety.reason: Rat lesion never compared in humans
safety.judgement: Kept safety on the Olney-lesion track because that is the model the FDA review relied on. The harms that did appear in patients (dissociation, sedation, blood-pressure rise, abuse; label section 5) were predicted from human volunteer studies (Krystal 1994), not from animals, so no rodent model was credited or contradicted for them. Traxoprodil produced an antidepressant response 'without also producing a dissociative reaction' (Preskorn 2008), consistent with rodent PCP-like behavioral screens, but no primary rodent source was verified so it was not used.
